name: armenia
facts: Yerevan, Armenia's capital, was founded in 782 BC, making it older than Rome.
Armenia has its own unique alphabet, still used today with 39 letters (Հայաստան is how you'd write 'Armenia' in it).
Armenia was the first country in the world to adopt Christianity as its state religion, in 301 AD.

name: austria
facts: Vienna was the capital of the Habsburg Empire for centuries, one of the most powerful royal families in European history.
Austria is home to the world's oldest zoo, Tiergarten Schönbrunn, opened in 1752.
Lake Neusiedl, on the border with Hungary, is one of the largest steppe lakes in Europe and barely a few meters deep.

name: bolivia
facts: Bolivia has two capitals, La Paz (administrative, and the highest in the world at over 3,600 meters) and Sucre (constitutional), a split that goes back to a civil war in 1899.
Lake Titicaca, shared with Peru, is the highest navigable lake in the world.
Bolivia is named after Simón Bolívar, the revolutionary leader who helped liberate several South American countries from Spanish rule.

name: mali
facts: Bogolan, or 'mudcloth', is a Malian fabric traditionally dyed using fermented mud, and its patterns are still used in fashion worldwide today.
Mansa Musa, a former ruler of the Mali Empire, is often cited as the richest person in history, thanks to the empire's gold and salt trade.
Mali is known for its distinct mudbrick architecture, especially the Great Mosque of Djenné, the largest mudbrick building in the world.

name: brazil
facts: Brazil is home to about 60% of the Amazon rainforest, the largest tropical rainforest in the world.
Brasília, Brazil's capital, was built from scratch in the 1950s to shift development toward the country's interior, and its layout looks like an airplane from above.
Christ the Redeemer, the famous statue in Rio, has been struck by lightning several times and even had a finger damaged once.

name: denmark
facts: Denmark has a strong concept called 'hygge', roughly meaning coziness and contentment, deeply embedded in daily Danish culture.
Denmark is one of the oldest continuous monarchies in the world, with a royal lineage tracing back over 1,000 years.
Denmark includes Greenland and the Faroe Islands as autonomous territories, making its total area far larger than mainland Denmark alone.

name: vietnam
facts: Vietnam uses a Latin-based alphabet (chữ Quốc ngữ) instead of Chinese characters, unlike many neighboring countries with similar historical scripts.
Motorbikes vastly outnumber cars in Vietnam, and are the primary mode of transport for most of the population.
Vietnam has one of the most narrow country shapes in the world, at some points less than 50 km wide.

name: kyrgyzstan
facts: Kyrgyzstan's flag features a 40-ray sun with a tunduk (the wooden crown of a yurt) at its center, symbolizing the 40 original Kyrgyz tribes.
Golden eagle hunting, known as berkutchi, is an ancient Kyrgyz tradition still practiced today, especially near Lake Issyk-Kul, where hunters train their eagles from a young age.
The Epic of Manas, Kyrgyzstan's national epic poem, runs to roughly 500,000 lines, about 20 times longer than Homer's Iliad and Odyssey combined.

name: germany
facts: Germany's Autobahn is famous for having no general speed limit on many stretches, though about 30% of the network does have posted limits.
Munich's Oktoberfest is the world's largest beer festival, drawing around 6 million visitors each year despite lasting just over two weeks.
Cologne Cathedral took 632 years to build, with construction starting in 1248 and finally finishing in 1880 after a nearly 300-year pause.

name: gabon
facts: Gabon's capital, Libreville, was founded in 1849 by freed slaves rescued from a captured slave ship, its name literally meaning 'Free Town.'
Around 85-90% of Gabon is covered in rainforest, making it one of the most forested countries in the world.
Gabon supplies around 90% of the world's okoumé, a lightweight tropical wood so central to the country's identity that it appears on the national coat of arms.

name: new zealand
facts: New Zealand sits atop a mostly submerged continent called Zealandia, of which about 94% lies underwater, with New Zealand forming the visible tip.
New Zealand has roughly 5 sheep for every person today, though the ratio once peaked at over 20 sheep per person in the 1980s.
New Zealand became the first self-governing country in the world to grant women the right to vote in parliamentary elections, in 1893.

name: kenya
facts: Kenya's Kalenjin community, from the Rift Valley highlands, has produced a disproportionate number of the world's elite long-distance runners, many training at high altitude in the town of Iten.
Mount Kenya, Africa's second-highest peak at 5,199 meters, is an extinct volcano and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Nairobi National Park is the only national park in the world located within a capital city, where lions and rhinos roam with the city skyline as a backdrop.

name: romania
facts: Bran Castle in Transylvania is popularly nicknamed 'Dracula's Castle,' inspired by the legend of Vlad the Impaler, though Bram Stoker's Dracula never actually stayed there.
The Danube Delta, formed just before the river reaches the Black Sea, is one of Europe's largest and best-preserved river deltas, covering roughly 2,200 square miles of wetlands and reed islands.
The statue of Dacian king Decebalus, carved directly into a riverside cliff along the Danube, stands 40 meters tall, making it the tallest rock sculpture in Europe.
